raw_case_text:
The 38-year-old female patient, who had no known systemic disease other than lumbar disc herniation and cervical disc herniation, sought medical care at a state hospital in the Eastern Black Sea region of Turkey with complaints of weakness, widespread muscle pain, unmeasured fever, night sweats, loss of appetite, and redness in the face and neck region for about a week. The laboratory examinations revealed that the patient had elevated acute phase reactants and renal function tests. The patient was then referred to the Giresun University Training and Research Hospital with a preliminary diagnosis of vasculitis. The patient's vital signs measured in the hospital's emergency department were as follows: arterial blood pressure: 100/60 mmHg, oxygen saturation (sO2): 95%, pulse in sinus rhythm: 100/min, and temperature: 36.7  C. The physical examination found that her general condition was moderate, and she was conscious, cooperative, and oriented. There was a V-shaped erythematous rash accompanied by increased temperature in the neck and the buccal region of the face bilaterally. The patient's lung sounds were normal. No tenderness or defense-rebound positivity was observed with palpation of the abdomen. There was also no bilateral pretibial edema.
The patient's lab parameters at the time of admission are shown in Table 1. These findings revealed a mild metabolic acidosis along with mild neutrophil leukocytosis, normocytic anemia, severely increased acute phase reactants such as erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and ferritin, moderately increased creatinine, and decreased B12 levels. Other lab test results were within normal range, such as INR, TSH, urinalysis, liver enzymes, electrolytes, and ELISA tests.
The posteroanterior chest X-ray and non-contrast abdominal tomography performed in the emergency department did not indicate any pathological finding that could explain the patient's clinical presentation. The patient was then hospitalized for differential diagnosis and treatment in the internal medicine service. The patient was prescribed isotonic fluid therapy for the possible prerenal cause of renal damage and 2 g/day IV ceftriaxone therapy for the potential bacterial infection. Infectious disease consultation revealed a recommendation for rheumatology consultation, suggesting that the possible underlying cause was considered rheumatologic rather than infectious. However, the rheumatological workup revealed no sign of vasculitic or auto-inflammatory disease (Table 1).
A more comprehensive anamnesis found that the patient who lives in the district center visited the village frequently and interacted with animals. The patient informed us that she had contact with chickens, cats, and dogs a week before the symptoms started. Serological tests for possible hantavirus infection and MAT test for possible Leptospira infection were requested for the patient under the coordination of Giresun Provincial Health Directorate. The results of the serological tests for hantavirus were negative. On the other hand, the leptospira MAT test performed at the Spirochet Diseases Diagnosis Laboratory of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Veterinary Control Central Research Institute revealed antibodies against L. interrogans serovar Bratislava type strain Jez Bratislava at 1/800 titer in the patient (Figure 1). Thus, a definitive diagnosis of leptospirosis was made. MAT was negative for other Leptospira serovars (Figure 1). Since ceftriaxone is one of the treatment choices in leptospirosis, and the patient's clinical findings were improving with the help of supportive treatments, no additional therapy was applied. The patient was discharged on the fifth day of hospitalization.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old female presenting with a one-week history of weakness, generalized muscle pain, fever, night sweats, anorexia, and facial and neck erythema.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began approximately one week prior to admission with progressive generalized weakness, diffuse myalgias, unmeasured fever, drenching night sweats, anorexia, and an erythematous rash on the face and neck. Initial evaluation at a regional hospital showed elevated acute phase reactants and renal dysfunction, prompting transfer under a presumptive diagnosis of systemic vasculitis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Lumbar disc herniation and cervical disc herniation; no other systemic illnesses. Epidemiological exposure: resides in a district center, travels frequently to a rural village with direct contact with chickens, cats, and dogs one week prior to symptom onset.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports weakness, generalized myalgia, unmeasured fever, night sweats, anorexia, and erythematous rash on the face and neck. Home medications: not documented. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, heart rate 100 beats/min (sinus rhythm), SpO2 95%, body temperature 36.7 °C. General: moderate general condition, conscious, cooperative, and oriented. Skin: V-shaped erythematous rash with localized warmth over the neck and bilateral buccal facial regions. Lungs: normal breath sounds bilaterally. Abdomen: soft, non-tender, no defense or rebound tenderness. Extremities: no pretibial edema bilaterally.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count revealed mild neutrophil leukocytosis and normocytic anemia. Acute phase reactants markedly elevated: severely increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and ferritin. Renal and metabolic panel showed moderate elevation in serum creatinine, mild metabolic acidosis, and decreased vitamin B12 levels. Normal laboratory parameters: INR, TSH, urinalysis, liver enzymes, electrolytes, and ELISA viral screens. Posteroanterior chest X-ray showed no pathological findings.
objective.advanced_workup: Non-contrast abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan: no pathological findings. Comprehensive rheumatologic panel: negative for vasculitic or autoinflammatory diseases.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Leptospirosis presenting with acute febrile illness, V-shaped erythematous facial and neck rash mimicking systemic vasculitis, acute renal impairment, and marked systemic inflammation. Confirmed by Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT) showing diagnostic antibody titer of 1/800 against Leptospira interrogans serovar Bratislava (type strain Jez Bratislava); MAT negative for other Leptospira serovars. Differential diagnoses ruled out: hantavirus serologies negative; autoimmune and vasculitic serologic workup negative.
Plan & Treatment: Intravenous isotonic crystalloid fluid hydration for prerenal azotemia and intravenous ceftriaxone 2 g/day for targeted antibacterial therapy; supportive care.
Outcome: Clinical symptoms and inflammatory markers rapidly improved; renal function normalized; discharged home in improved condition on hospital day 5.
